language_wrapper: On the faces of a regular {solid_name}, the numbers 1 through {n_faces} are randomly written, one distinct number per face. Two numbers a and b are called {t_window}-consecutive if their circular distance modulo {n_faces} is at most {t_window} (in particular, 1 and {n_faces} are {t_window}-consecutive). What is the value of m + n, where m/n (in lowest terms) is the probability that no two {t_window}-consecutive numbers are written on faces that share an edge?
hardness_rationale: The seed problem forbids only immediate circular neighbors (distance 1) on the octahedron. This family both (i) varies the underlying face-adjacency graph (octahedron or cube), altering symmetry and constraint interactions, and (ii) strengthens the local restriction to circular distance at most t, which couples many more edges simultaneously. Counting now requires handling an injective labeling under nonlocal edge constraints: direct symmetry arguments or inclusion–exclusion over a nontrivial graph, or an exact enumeration with pruning. The interplay between the graph structure and the modular distance threshold makes quick guessing or simple heuristics ineffective.
notes: Generalized family and proof of correctness: We view the face-adjacency structure of a regular solid as a graph G whose vertices are faces. A labeling is a bijection f: V(G) -> {1,2,...,n}, where n is the number of faces. Two labels a,b are declared t-consecutive if their circular distance modulo n is at most t; that is, min(|a-b|, n - |a-b|) <= t. A labeling is valid if for every edge uv in G, the labels f(u) and f(v) are not t-consecutive. Since every labeling is equally likely, the desired probability equals (number of valid labelings)/(n!). For the cube, the face-adjacency graph is the octahedron graph (six vertices, all edges except the three opposite pairs). For the octahedron, the face-adjacency graph is the cube graph (eight vertices, edges between vertices at Hamming distance 1 in {0,1}^3). The verifier computes the numerator by exact enumeration over all n! bijections and checks the constraint for each edge—this is correct by definition of the probability space and the constraint. Nontriviality is enforced by rejecting instances whose probability is 0 or 1. For paper solutions, one may use inclusion–exclusion across the set of forbidden edge adjacencies, or exploit the automorphism group of G to reduce cases; strengthening to t >= 2 induces larger forbidden neighborhoods in the cyclic metric, increasing the complexity of compatible labelings and necessitating more advanced counting than the original seed.
source_question: The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are randomly written on the faces of a regular octahedron so that each face contains a different number.  The probability that no two consecutive numbers, where 8 and 1 are considered to be consecutive, are written on faces that share an edge is $m/n,$ where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers.  Find $m + n.$
